Docs The feature card

the entity in one handle, one analogy and one constraint box

Authored in cards/statement.md — the only hand-written source on this page. Everything counted elsewhere is read from the codebase at build time.

“The bank's list against your list — matched lines staple shut.”

ISThe statement pipeline — a PDF cartola in → layout-routed extraction (deterministic for known banks, Gemini fallback for unknown) → typed lines → a deterministic reconciliation run that verdicts every line against the receipt ledger → MATCHED pairs lock the paired transaction.
IS NOTThe receipt scan (that is scan-receipt's pipeline), the transaction record itself, or the card-alias registry — the statement CONSUMES aliases and FREEZES transactions; it owns neither.
DECIDESWhich transactions the bank has confirmed (and are therefore frozen), which statement lines have no receipt, and which receipts never hit the statement.

An auditor who takes the bank's cartola in one hand and your shoebox of receipts in the other, and works down the bank's list line by line: same date, same amount → staple the pair together; a line with no receipt goes in one tray, a receipt with no line in another, and a line that could match two receipts gets a question mark instead of a guess. Stapled pairs are frozen — nobody edits a number the bank has already confirmed. Throw the cartola away and every staple comes out.

AnalogyIn this codebase
upload the cartolaPOST /statements (PDF ≤25MB · optional card alias · optional password)
the auditor readingstatement_routing (known layouts, PyMuPDF deterministic) or statement_profile_fallback + statement_pdf_evidence (unknown layouts, Gemini)
cleaning the handwritingstatement_coalesce (shared Gemini normalization)
the line-by-line matchstatement_reconciliation._score_line_candidate (date + amount tolerances, reasons recorded)
the staplethe paired transaction locks (P117)
reading aloud as they goSSE /statements/{id}/events + WS /ws/statements/{id}
the locked drawer's keyDELETE /statements/{id} — verdicts cascade away, rows unlock

Easy to confuse:

  • statement vs receipt — the cartola is the BANK's record; the receipt is YOURS. Reconciliation is the meeting; neither replaces the other.
  • reconcile vs lock — the verdict is the finding; the lock is its consequence on the TRANSACTION (a matched row refuses edits, transaction territory).
  • password_required vs failed — an encrypted PDF parks at PASSWORD_REQUIRED and resubmits through /process with the password; FAILED is the pipeline giving up.

Where the analogy stops working: Verdicts are per reconciliation RUN — re-running re-verdicts idempotently; a user's manual edit takes precedence over a re-run (D50).

Full card — what & why, for whom, flows, is / is not

What & Why

The statement is the ledger's second witness. Receipts say what you bought; the cartola says what the bank charged. This entity turns an uploaded PDF statement into typed lines and then RECONCILES them against the receipt ledger — deterministically, with a verdict per line — so agreement becomes visible and disagreement becomes a work list.

The pipeline (D49). POST /statements takes a PDF (≤25MB, daily rate-limited), optionally pinned to a card alias and carrying a password for encrypted cartolas. The worker routes the layout: a KNOWN bank statement parses deterministically with PyMuPDF (statement_routing — explicit routing evidence recorded); an unknown layout falls back to Gemini over compact rows plus a layout profile (statement_profile_fallback + statement_pdf_evidence), normalized by the shared coalesce rules (D55's statement-only prompt lab guards this path with a 50-case corpus). Lines land typed (StatementLineType: charge · payment · interest · fee · insurance · tax · adjustment · other), and progress streams over SSE and WS the whole way.

The reconciliation (D50). POST /{id}/reconcile runs the deterministic engine: each statement line is scored against candidate receipt transactions on date (within a configured day tolerance) and amount (amount-scaled tolerance), with the REASONS recorded (same_date, exact_amount, amount_tolerance:N…) — the chips a human sees on the lock popup. One candidate → MATCHED; none → STATEMENT_ONLY; a receipt no line claims → RECEIPT_ONLY; two candidates → AMBIGUOUS, never a guess. Re-runs are idempotent and user edits take precedence.

The consequence (P117). A MATCHED verdict freezes the paired transaction — content locked, badge shown, edits refused with the rule named. DELETE /statements/{id} is the escape hatch: lines, runs and verdicts cascade away and every locked row unlocks.

An auditor stapling the bank's list to your receipts, tray by tray — and every staple names its reason.

For Whom

The user who wants to know "did the bank charge me what my receipts say?" without reading two lists side by side — and who must be TOLD when a line has no receipt, not shown a silent hole. The cost-conscious operator: unknown-layout extraction spends Gemini money, so the deterministic known-bank path and the prompt-lab gate are load-bearing. And the developer: a financial pipeline whose verdicts are deterministic and reasoned, whose reruns are idempotent, and whose lock side-effects have a named escape hatch.

Flows

  • upload ★ → a PDF cartola → POST /statements (≤25MB · optional card alias · optional password) → the worker routes the layout → typed lines land → EXTRACTED
  • password → an encrypted cartola parks at PASSWORD_REQUIRED / PASSWORD_INVALID → resubmit through POST /{id}/process with the password
  • watch → SSE /statements/{id}/events (or WS /ws/statements/{id}) streams upload → extracting → extracted → reconciling
  • browse → the Cartolas list — StatementCard grammar (identity · period · status pill · per-row delete · coverage bar from line/matched counts) + the 4-step upload stepper
  • reconcile ★ → POST /{id}/reconcile → the deterministic engine verdicts every line: MATCHED · STATEMENT_ONLY · RECEIPT_ONLY · AMBIGUOUS — with reasons
  • lock → a MATCHED verdict freezes the paired transaction (P117) → badge on the row/detail · edits refused with the rule named
  • delete → DELETE /{id} → lines, runs and verdicts cascade away → matched transactions UNLOCK (the escape hatch)

Is

  • the upload pipeline: POST /statements (PDF-only, 25MB cap, daily rate limit) → statement_worker → layout routing (deterministic PyMuPDF for known banks, routing evidence recorded) or the Gemini fallback (compact rows + layout profile + coalesce normalization)
  • typed lines: StatementLineType — charge · payment · interest · fee · insurance · tax · adjustment · other
  • the deterministic reconciliation engine: per-line candidate scoring on date + amount tolerances, reasons recorded, AMBIGUOUS over a guess, idempotent re-runs, user-edit precedence (D50)
  • the lock consequence: a MATCHED verdict freezes the paired transaction (P117); GET /transactions/{id}/lock-links names this statement line from the transaction's side
  • the escape hatch: DELETE /statements/{id} cascades lines/runs/verdicts and unlocks matched rows; the stored PDF is removed best-effort
  • encrypted cartolas: PASSWORD_REQUIRED / PASSWORD_INVALID park the statement; POST /{id}/process resubmits with the password (409 outside re-processable states)
  • live progress: SSE /statements/{id}/events + WS /ws/statements/{id}
  • the GS4 card grammar: per-statement (line_count, matched_line_count) in one grouped query → the list's coverage bar
  • the D55 guard: a statement-only Gemini prompt lab (50-case corpus in junit) gates the fallback extraction path

Is Not

  • not the receipt scan — scanning a cartola IMAGE was the w6-era surface; today's statement enters as a PDF upload, and the receipt pipeline belongs to scan-receipt
  • not the transaction's lock UI — the badge, the popup and the refused edit render on transaction surfaces; this entity supplies the VERDICT that causes them
  • not the card-alias registry — aliases are their own entity (D48: alias-only, a PCI boundary; no PAN is ever stored); a statement merely pins to one
  • not a bank connection — the cartola arrives by hand as a PDF; nothing polls a bank API
  • reconciliation is not collaborative review — one owner's ledger against one owner's statement (D50's scale row defers more)

why the entity behaves the way it does

Source: the entity card's DECIDED section. A decision here is a rule the code obeys, not a plan — the ones with ids are in .kdbp/DECISIONS.md.

DecisionWhat it settles
D48card alias + statement schema foundation: financial data, ownership scope, RLS, and a PCI boundary — aliases stay alias-only, statements ownership-scoped
D49PDF upload + extraction worker: async worker, file persistence, failure states, streaming progress
D50reconciliation engine: deterministic verdicts, idempotent reruns, ambiguity handled by verdict (never a guess), user-edit precedence
D51 / D52web + Android statement flows: upload/progress/buckets as primary user-facing workflows
D53exit gate: full deployed journey + financial edge cases; 200-line statement bound
D54corpus + contract preflight: private PDFs, encrypted/password paths, no-PCI output contract before runtime work
D55statement-only Gemini prompt lab + coalesce gate before provider promotion
P117lock-on-match: a MATCHED verdict freezes the paired transaction; delete is the escape hatch
D97 (consequence)the deterministic staging-e2e fixture backend is gone; the full-journey e2e spec is QUARANTINED until a scan-mock restores determinism (Launch Readiness)

DB entities and API shapes — each names its file and the endpoints that touch it

A field typed with another documented class LINKS to it (violet) instead of repeating its structure. Examples are synthetic — derived from Literal values and field-name heuristics, never real user data.
Type colors — one hue per family, deeper = the wider type: int float · Decimal numeric · date · time datetime temporal · str bytes · Text textual · bool · list · dict · Literal structured · UUID identity · None nullable. An uncolored token is a domain alias (an enum defined in this codebase).
Insight icons — the DATA-MODEL lens; the same shape runs over other member kinds later (functions · methods), scoped, never mixed:
  • model — a persisted DB entity: lives in a table, owns FKs.
  • schema — an API / pipeline shape: crosses a boundary, owns no storage.
  • base — derives from NOTHING: no FK out, no field typed by another documented class; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-class flag — field count ≥ 15; the number that makes it a split candidate below.
  • Class N% closest structural twin — % = shared fields over the union (Jaccard); a ≥80% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • orphan — zero API usage AND zero internal references; becomes a deprecation candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoint touches + FK in) · violet = internal (mapped backend files referencing the class). Api-silent is not dead; only a true orphan is.

Kind colors: integration API through HTTP · unit components in isolation · journey real browser flows · coverage lines executed · manual a human walked it · deployed probes against the live app

Six angles can verify this entity; the api corpus does, richly — the web unit angle is thin and named so. Every count on this page is read from junit at build time; the lines below say only what each kind is for here.

KindWhat it is for on this entity
integrationthe pipeline through pytest: upload endpoint (types, size, rate limit, password states), the worker, layout routing + deterministic parsing, coalesce normalization, the profile fallback, the reconciliation engine's verdict classes (exact · tolerance · discount · tax · fails · edge cases), lock-on-match, the matched flag, SSE + WS endpoints, models, and the D55 prompt-lab corpus.
unitthe web side in isolation: the statements route render; the StatementCard/StatementStepper components ride the route test — a thin slice, named as such.
journeyfour specs on disk (statement-journey · statement-reconcile · gs4-statements-grammar · w6-scan-statements); D121 keeps web e2e local-only, and the FULL journey spec is quarantined (D97: no deterministic backend) — its committed shots carry the visual claim.
coveragethe repo pytest --cov gate (≥80%) passes but is not sliced per entity; a per-path slice is the growth step.
manualan operator walking the built feature into walks.jsonl. No statement walk exists yet — this adoption's approval will be the first.
deployedprobes against the live statement API. Nothing machine-readable watches the deployed pipeline today.

A set is one directory under tests/web-e2e/proof/; its manifest.json supplies the story and the leg names, the file counts are walked off disk. The ROLE column says where each set sits in the entity's story — derived from the card's # FLOWS and the manifest (an explicit role:/flows: in the manifest overrides the inference; an inferred role says so). A ★ in the card's FLOWS marks the GOLDEN PATH — this feature's own main journey; a set covering a ★ flow wears the star, and an unproven ★ flow is the loudest gap on the shelf. Open a row to see its legs, then click any artifact to open the viewer — ← / → or the side arrows run through the WHOLE set, leg by leg; ↑ / ↓ move to the previous or next set (folding this one shut and unfolding that one); Esc closes. Opening or closing a set cascades to its legs.
Role: principal ★ main workflow · ★ = golden path · edge guards · degraded · destructive · reference design-lab fidelity, not proof · supporting context · unclassified / unproven needs clarification, or a flow with no set — both feed Pending
Row states: artifacts on disk this build · empty / absent declared for this entity but nothing to show — a named gap

What this set shows: The encrypted cartola's guard rail walked on production: uploaded without its password, the statement parks at contraseña requerida before any extraction — the recent-list card wears the pill and the Protegida lock, and the StatusPanel offers the inline unlock form. A wrong password re-queues it, and the verdict arrives over the stream: one frame catches the card already flipped to contraseña incorrecta while the panel still reads en cola — two surfaces mid-stream, no reload anywhere. The terminal state persists on the card until the capture's own uploads are swept away.

live capture, 2026-07-23 — an encrypted twin of the e2e fixture (pypdf, password withheld) walked on production (:5174 prod-e2e, user B, es-CL, mobile-390). ZERO Gemini: the API detects encryption SYNCHRONOUSLY at upload and the wrong-password verdict comes from the decryption attempt — nothing ever reached the extraction stage. Every capture upload was deleted afterwards (the backend dedupes identical files by sha, so the walk resolves to one statement). The resubmit-with-CORRECT-password half is junit's (TestStatementUploadEndpoint password cases); walking it live would hand the PDF to real Gemini (D97). Side-finding logged: the upload screen's post-success auto-navigate does not fire — the user stays on the form.
